items.quote: self:SetScript("OnUpdate", function()
items.what: WFA-13: an OnUpdate runs every frame the world map is open, even with the cursor still
items.why: WFA-13: 'no idle OnUpdate'. The area pin polls the cursor each frame (HoverAt -> Model.AreaAt) whenever the map shows a zone with shaded areas; it stops only when the map closes. The comment gives the reason (a mouse-enabled frame would swallow map clicks), so the fix may be cheap early-out (skip when GetCursorPosition is unchanged) rather than removal; work is bounded, hence low.
items.reason: Replace or explicitly waive stationary-cursor polling, preserving map clicks, pan/zoom hover and immediate highlight clearing under WFA-13? The OnUpdate closure stays installed on visible area pins and calls canvas focus/cursor-coordinate APIs every frame even when the canvas cursor has not changed; the early-out skips HoverAt only. WFA-13 forbids idle OnUpdate, and the repository has no waiver; polling avoids swallowing map clicks and responds to pan/zoom, so any replacement must preserve those requirements and needs an owner timing/input decision.

items.quote: - **Zone completion**: how much of a zone's Legacy objectives you've done, Guild Wars 2 style. Out of the box it counts areas explored (each is a step of the zone's Explore achievement, toward Explorer) for the character, and dungeons, raids and the zone's other Legacy objectives for your Legacy progress on the account. Flight paths learned and local reputations at Friendly aren't Legacy objectives; tick them under "What counts" to count them too. So can quests, if you have [Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie) installed: the zone's quests your character can take, read from Questie's database in game. A zone reaching 100% of what you count gets a toast and a sound, and continent maps show how many of the continent's zones are complete. It shows in the world map's corner, for the zone you're viewing, and in each zone badge's tooltip on continent maps; unticking "On the world map" in the map menu hides both the corner and the continent badges. It can also show in the objective tracker, for the zone you're in (the zone name, a percentage and one row of counts), once you tick that in the map menu. Each can be collapsed, and hovering lists what's left. "What counts" in the same menu adds or leaves out any category, and the percentage and the toast follow.
items.what: one feature bullet of ~230 words across 10 sentences; "What counts" explained twice
items.why: Owner decision (player-facing copy): keep the first two sentences plus where it shows and the 100% toast; the per-category detail already lives in docs/zone-completion.md (linked two sections below), and docs/curseforge.md says the same in ~60 words. The Tracker bullet (line 22, ~140 words) has the same shape.
items.reason: same producer as d5636854d7: the same README Zone completion bullet, tracked there under WFA-10

items.quote:
local function Attach(trackerModule)
	if ForeverTrackerHost then
		ForeverTrackerHost.Attach(trackerModule)
		return
	end
	-- The shared private host is optional; standalone companions stay inert until it loads.
end

local function AttachAll()
	for _, trackerModule in ipairs(modules) do
		Attach(trackerModule)
	end
end

---@param trackerModule LegacyTrackerModule
---@return boolean
local function IsAttached(trackerModule)
	if ForeverTrackerHost then
		return ForeverTrackerHost.IsAttached(trackerModule)
	end
	return false
end
items.what: Attach and IsAttached wrappers guard a missing ForeverTrackerHost for 'standalone companions' that are not in this repo
items.why: TrackerHost.lua loads before Tracker.lua in the TOC and defines the global whenever ObjectiveTrackerFrame exists; Tracker.AddModule returns nil before Attach when the tracker is unavailable, so the nil branch (empty Attach fallthrough, IsAttached returning false) never runs in the shipped addon. Only the lifecycle spec sets the global by hand. Collapsed: call ns.TrackerHost.Attach / IsAttached directly.

items.quote: local function Layout()
items.what: Layout is a ~140-line function (164-302) with distinct phases: combat lift above the native slot (166-210), Edit Mode bail-out, module stacking (215-250), off-screen shift (251-280), native viewport height sync (281-301).
items.why: Each phase touches shared upvalues (nativeAnchor, requestedNativeHeight, appliedNativeHeight) but could be a named local (LiftForCombat, StackModules, ClampNativeHeight). The combat and normal paths are what the owner's uncommitted edit is growing, so the split is best done as its own reviewed change after the anchor helper above.
items.reason: The phases form one synchronous layout transaction: the initial anchor determines available height, module updates determine host height, that height changes CENTER/BOTTOM top geometry and off-screen shift, and the final bottom constrains the native viewport while requested/applied heights prevent drift. Combat and Edit Mode short-circuit the same transaction; naming helpers may aid reading but the cited phases do not establish independent responsibilities or a size defect.
